decisions.reason: As a component that builds directly on the firm's established radiant-heater know-how, service capabilities and manufacturing base, it remains more likely to be improved and retained than withdrawn, even if it is less strategic than the flagship lines.

The electric infrared panel-heater line fits the firm's low-carbon direction, draws on closely related heating and systems knowledge, and is therefore highly likely to stay on the market and be refined through in-house R&D.

The electric halogen infrared heater is close enough to the firm's core knowledge to be supported, but its less central strategic role and likely overlap with stronger electric lines make it the most exposed to future portfolio pruning.

This industrial electric infrared hall-heater line is very close to the firm's established application expertise in large non-residential spaces, so accumulated market feedback can be absorbed and used to strengthen rather than abandon it.

The hydrogen-capable gas dark infrared heater is strongly aligned with the firm's stated hydrogen-ready path and rests on highly related combustion and infrared-heating capabilities, making withdrawal very unlikely.
